pages.text:
Wukong and Ao Bing find a little green
leaf under the peach tree. “This leaf
wants a boat ride!” says Wukong. Sandy
fills a clear tub halfway with water, and
he sets it on the low table.
2

Wukong rolls a lump of orange clay into a
round ball. “Here is your boat, little leaf!”
he says. He sets the clay ball on the
water and lets go.
3

Plop! The clay ball sinks all the way to
the bottom of the tub. Wukong stares
down through the clear water. The little
leaf is still on the table, waiting for
its ride.
4

“Ao Bing, can your dragon magic make it
float?” asks Wukong. Ao Bing smiles and
shakes his head. “We don’t need magic,”
he says. “Let’s try with our hands and see
what happens.”
5

Wukong lifts the dripping clay out of the
tub. “It is still the same clay,” says Ao
Bing. “We will not add any or take any
away. Let’s change its shape instead.”
6

Together they press the ball flat and
wide, like a big pancake. “A pancake
boat!” laughs Wukong. “It is so much
wider than the ball. Let’s test it on
the water!”
7

The flat clay sinks too, slowly, slowly,
down to the bottom. The water slides
right over its flat top. “Hmm,” says Ao
Bing. “It needs edges to keep the
water out.”
8

They change the shape again. They pinch
up the edges, all the way around, until
the clay looks like a little bowl. Now the
middle is hollow, and the sides stand
up high.
9

They set the clay boat gently on the
water to test it again. This time it bobs
on top! “It floats!” shouts Wukong, and he
throws both arms up in the air.
10

“It is the same clay,” says Ao Bing, “but
now it has a hollow shape.” The wide,
hollow boat pushes aside lots of water,
and the water holds it up. Sandy smiles
and says, “That was a good test!”
11

Wukong sets the little leaf in the boat.
The high edges keep the water out, so
the leaf stays dry. “Every good boat
needs a name,” says Ao Bing. “What
should we call this one?”
12

Wukong looks up at the peach tree to
find a good name. The peaches up there
are round, just like the little boat. “I will
call it the Big Peach!” he says.
13

Ao Bing laughs. “A big name is fine for a
little boat,” he says. “But a real big
peach would never fit inside it!” Wukong
laughs too, and he smiles at his tiny boat.
14

Wukong leans close to the tub and blows
softly on the boat. Whoosh! The Big
Peach glides all the way across the water
to the other side. The little leaf rides
along and stays dry.
15

Sandy picks a real peach from the tree.
“This big peach is for us to eat,” he says,
“not for the boat!” Everyone laughs, and
the little leaf keeps sailing in the
Big Peach.
16
